messages:
eva-support: FYI cust-427 just hit a runtime error — their embedding index asserts because the vector length changed after they pinned our model variant. They pinned open-embed-v3@2026-02-20. Previously vectors were 1024, now API returns 768. Attaching sample response below.

cust-427 (paste):
```
{
  \"request_id\": \"req_01GXYZ\",\n  \"model\": \"open-embed-v3@2026-02-20\",\n  \"embedding\": [0.001, -0.02, ...],\n  \"embedding_length\": 768\n}
```

eva-support: Error in their index creation: \"expected vec length 1024, got 768\". They only started seeing this after the pinned change. Can ops/infra check routing and variant mapping? :eyes:

sanjay: Got it. Can you paste the full request payload headers and the request_id from their logs (req_01GXYZ good). Also which endpoint (text-embed-ada style or /v1/embeddings)?

eva-support: They call POST /v1/embeddings with model: \"open-embed-v3\" (pinned to that variant in UI). Headers include x-redwood-client: cust-427, auth ok. I ran a quick curl using their request_id but obfuscated.

maya: Quick hypothesis: when a variant is pinned we still allow fallback to a compatible variant alias if the pinned variant isn't present in the serving pool. Fallback could map to a smaller-dim variant. Need to confirm whether pinned binding prevents that.

deploy-bot: [deploy event] 2026-02-20T03:12:44Z - canary: open-embed-v3@2026-02-20 deployed to pool-3, variant-tag: quantized-q8_768

kai: That deploy note looks suspicious — quantized-q8_768 would explain 768-length vectors. If the model was swapped to a quantized 768 variant as a fallback it could return shorter length.

sanjay: Reproducing locally now. curl I used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-v3@2026-02-20","input":"test"}'
```

sanjay: Repro successful. With the pinned variant string we still got a response with embedding_length: 768. Looks like router handed the request to a quantized variant that is API-compatible but different vector width. :confused:

maya: Two actions: 1) stop automatic fallback to variants with different embedding widths for pinned customers (hotfix), 2) provide a compatibility check during pinning UI to warn if the pinned variant changes vector dimensionality.

opsbot: Alert created: #ALERT-5643 - \"pin-fallback-veclen-mismatch\". Assigned to eng-runtime.

kai: Short-term mitigation for cust-427: re-pin to the last-known 1024 variant (open-embed-v3@2025-11-12) or roll back the 2026-02-20 deployment from pool-3. I'll prepare a rollback playbook. :hammer_and_wrench:

maya: Also need a migration note: when quantization reduces vector width we must surface this in the model catalog under \"breaking changes\". Some customers rely on fixed vec lengths for indexes.

sanjay: For troubleshooting, I collected the router trace for req_01GXYZ: router->pool-3->variant: open-embed-v3@2026-02-20-quant-q8_768 (fallback). Attaching trace id trace_9b4.

eva-support: Shared trace and reproduction steps with cust-427, they confirmed they can repro and blocked ingest. They asked for ETA.

maya: Estimating: hotfix to disallow cross-width fallbacks = low-risk patch, rolling out to staging in 1 hour, canary to a subset of customers in 2-3 hours, full rollout after validation. If cust-427 needs immediate unblock, suggest rollback of the deploy in pool-3.

sanjay: Created PR that adds a strict-compat check in router: variants are compatible only if embedding_size matches exactly. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/3214.

kai: Ops will schedule rollback in next maintenance window unless customer requests immediate rollback. For now put cust-427 on accelerated support queue and offer temporary ingest pause + manual backfill later.

eva-support: Customer accepted rollback option. Marking thread for follow-up once rollback completes. :white_check_mark:
